body:
Retested sections 1, 3 and 4 on 1.4.7 (Windows 11, `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, isolated CLI homes without my plugins).

Section 1, tool calls issued together: still serial. In one model step the model issued three `run_command` calls, each sleeping 6 s and printing a timestamp. The printed times were `16:40:34.009`, `16:40:41.488` and `16:40:48.956`, 7.5 s apart, and the step durations were 8.3, 15.7 and 23.1 s, each one waiting for the previous. A second trial gave the same shape (14.4 s spread). In separate tests with sleeps of 2, 6 and 4 s, the durations were again cumulative, 4.1, 11.9 and 17.5 s, and the results were attached to the right calls.

One nuance I had not measured before: when the model gives each call a short `WaitMsBeforeAsync` (1,000 ms in my run), the commands go to the background and do overlap. Sleeps of 12, 9 and 15 s finished after 13.6, 11.7 and 19.3 s. So the serial behaviour shows up when the model waits a few seconds per call before backgrounding, which is what it chose in the runs above.

Section 3, headless overhead: better than I reported. Four runs gave 6.6 to 6.9 s of client overhead (wall time minus `duration_seconds`), compared with about 12 s in my report. About 5.3 s of that is before the prompt is sent: roughly 2.2 s for the silent auth and 2.6 s more before the user message goes out. These runs had no plugins, while my original runs had a 32.6k-token plugin prefix, so the two numbers are not a clean comparison.

Section 4, summary store: not comparable here. In a fresh home the store is about 650 bytes, not 943 KB. It is still rewritten whole (sizes 653, 656, 659, 656 bytes), but only 4 times in 46 s of an active run.
